questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place that I haven't been to before and a place that I found interesting

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, it helped that I had a fellow student going to the same university

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had an exchanges team that we could e-mail and we had a start orientation where we got to meet the other exchange students. Unfortunately this orientation did not provide us with any practical information like where to get books, how to find our classes, where to get supplies for the kitchen etc. it mainly focused on the social aspects.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were dorm rooms for 1, 2 or 3 people, apartments for around 6-7 people, town houses for either 3 or 6 people, family houses and grad houses which varied in size.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You could get a meal plan where you could buy all meals in the school cafeterias or at selected restaurants and get a 10% discount. You could also put minimum 300$ on your student card so you could purchase food when you wanted and still get a 10% discount. Some housing options did not provide a kitchen so you would have to get a meal plan, other housing options provide a fully equipped kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: The house/room you move into if very empty, you have to buy everything yourself. The kitchen only comes with a fridge, freezer, oven, stove and sink, you have to buy plates, cutlery, pots, pans etc., also sheets, pillows, blankets. We found some fairly cheap and okay quality stuff in Walmart or in thrift stores. The university do provide a service where you can rent kitchen stuff, but it was more expensive than buying all of it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Would have been 5, if it was possible to rent or buy stuff from the exchange students that stayed there prior.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: First you have to find 8-10 courses that you would like/have to take, you have to get a pre-approval of the courses from your home university before you can apply to register. You also have to make sure that you have taken the right courses at your home university that would give you access to the courses you wish to take at your host university. On top of that you have to make sure non of the courses overlap in the schedule both with lectures and with the final exams. Some courses require an approval from the professor, so you would need to fill out the approval from with help form the exchange team or the professor. Sometimes if the exchange team says they can not help you get into a course, try to contact the professor directly. After you made sure of all of the above, you can apply to register, you will get assigned to 4-5 courses, and you can change and drop courses in the start of the semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can e-mail the exchange team or the professors. They also provide a PDF guide on how to register for courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful, I got into the courses I wanted to

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not be afraid to contact the professors, they often want to help when you explain your situration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses was lower than expected, but I also took some 2nd and 3rd year courses where I probably could have taken 4th year courses. The final exams was a lot easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was similar, a lot of lectures, more and easier assignments at the host university than at UCPH, and less oral presentations at the host university. When grading assignments they would focus more on grammar and form than on the science, which I found very different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ANSC*4010 - Animal Welfare Judging & Evaluation
ANSC*4560 - Pet Nutrition
ZOO*2090 - Vertebrate Structure and Function
ANSC*3090 - Principles of Animal Behaviour

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Vertebrate Structure and Function, because it had laboratory exercises which is always fun, also it provides a good background knowledge about how all species are connected.

questions.answer: All the kitchen supplies and bedroom supplies you have to buy when you first move in

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were all sorts of clubs: k-pop, Caribbean community, indian community, muslim community, christian community, charity, innovation, international community, dance, soccer, swimming, rowing, book clubs, outdoors clubs, the list keeps going.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked going to the fitness center, and I enjoyed going to the events that the clubs put on.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going to Toronto, and to go to other provinces in the Canada, it is fairly cheap.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it really easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Do not be shy, maybe get involved in some clubs with a majority of local students or play sports.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: People are very polite and will small talk to you in class, but often they will be hesitant to talk to you outside of class. And remember to tip service people and they add tax to everything even thought it is not on the price tag.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How nice and friendly people are, and how open and accepting they are.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Do not be shy, go outside of your comfort zone and remember to have fun.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't think so

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the friendships and memories I made

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding time to do all the things I wanted to do, the times went by so fast.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
